# Feature CRUD Pattern

Use this pattern when adding a new CRUD feature.

Example feature name: products

## Files to create

src/types/products.ts
src/api/products.ts
src/pages/products/ProductsPage.tsx
src/pages/products/ProductFormPage.tsx

## Files to edit

src/api/index.ts
src/App.tsx
src/layouts/Sidebar.tsx

## Step 1 - Types

Create src/types/products.ts

Product:
- id: string
- name: string
- status: string
- created_at?: string
- updated_at?: string

ProductCreate:
- name: string
- status: string

## Step 2 - API functions

Create src/api/products.ts

Rules:
- import client from ./client
- import types from ../types/products
- return response.data
- do not return full Axios responses

Required functions:
- getProducts
- getProduct
- createProduct
- updateProduct
- deleteProduct

## Step 3 - List page

Create src/pages/products/ProductsPage.tsx

Rules:
- use PageHeader
- use LoadingSpinner
- use ErrorMessage
- use DataTable
- use StatusBadge where needed
- handle loading state
- handle error state
- handle empty state

Correct useApi pattern:

const { data, loading, error } = useApi(getProducts)

Do not pass a second dependency-array argument to useApi.

## Step 4 - Detail or edit page with route parameter

When using route params, wrap API calls with useCallback.

Correct pattern:

const loadProduct = useCallback(() => getProduct(id), [id])
const { data, loading, error } = useApi(loadProduct)

## Step 5 - Routes

Edit src/App.tsx

Example routes:

<Route path="products" element={<ProductsPage />} />
<Route path="products/new" element={<ProductFormPage />} />
<Route path="products/:id/edit" element={<ProductFormPage />} />

## Step 6 - Sidebar

Edit src/layouts/Sidebar.tsx

Add:

{ label: 'Products', path: '/products' }

Current sidebar items use only:
- label
- path

Do not add icon unless the Sidebar component is intentionally updated.

## Step 7 - Validation

Run:

npm run lint
npm run build

Both must pass.
